In which prostate cancer risk group does a bone scan for metastatic evaluation become recommended at the lowest risk level?
Answer Choices: (A) High risk (B) Very Low risk (C) Intermediate-High risk (D) Early Intermediate risk (E) Favorable Intermediate (F) Regional risk (G) Low risk (H) Low-Intermediate risk (I) Unfavorable Intermediate (J) Localized risk

Distinguish intermediate risk subgroups, especially unfavorable versus favorable intermediate risk, and cite guideline or authoritative evidence.'}

The lowest routine risk category at which **bone scan is considered for metastatic staging is unfavorable intermediate-risk (UIR)** prostate cancer—not favorable intermediate-risk (FIR).

- **AUA/ASTRO:** The retrieved guideline summary supports staging localized UIR disease with cross-sectional imaging and bone scintigraphy. A comparison of NCCN, AUA, and EAU recommendations also reports a more restrictive AUA bone-imaging threshold, so the precise recommendation can vary by guideline and version. [AUA/ASTRO recommendation summary; guideline-comparison study]
- **Favorable intermediate risk:** Routine staging imaging is generally not indicated; an appropriateness summary rates imaging as rarely appropriate for very-low-, low-, and FIR disease, while rating it appropriate for newly diagnosed UIR or higher-risk disease. [Appropriateness summary]
- **Practical takeaway:** For a general threshold, use **UIR** as the lowest category where bone imaging enters routine staging consideration. Do not treat intermediate risk as one uniform group; FIR is generally below that threshold. Check the current guideline version and individual clinical features when applying this to a patient.

Sources: [Guideline-comparison study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32691147/) and [PubMed search results on staging recommendations](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40493830/).

The search evidence identifies unfavorable intermediate-risk prostate cancer as the lowest category where bone scintigraphy enters routine staging consideration, while favorable intermediate risk generally does not.
